This book is writtn to serve a companion to a wide range of statistics text-books.The computer case studies are included at the end, so that this casebook an be at least partially self-contained. Programs are organized alphabetically rather than by topic, so that you can choose whichever programs you need. An instrutor may indicate the preferred order to use the programs. But as the title suggests you are encouraged to explore. There is no lock-step method here. You can sneak ahead. Although the writing style of this book assumes you are encurraged to explore. There is no lock-step method here. You can sneak ahead. Although the writing style of this book assumes you are a mature learner, it doesn't require you to be a mathematician or computer programmer. If you can read carefully and do simple algebra, you can handle the main ideas. Mathematical notation is minimal, to avoid conflict with your other textbook(s)
